definition: Document processing is a field of research and a set of production processes aimed at making an analog document digital.
details: Document processing does not simply aim to photograph or scan a document to obtain a digital image, but also to make it digitally intelligible. This includes extracting the structure of the document or the layout and then the content, which can take the form of text or images. The process can involve traditional computer vision algorithms, convolutional neural networks or manual labor. The problems addressed are related to semantic segmentation, object detection, optical character recognition (OCR), handwritten text recognition (HTR) and, more broadly, transcription, whether automatic or not. The term can also include the phase of digitizing the document using a scanner and the phase of interpreting the document, for example using natural language processing (NLP) or image classification technologies. It is applied in many industrial and scientific fields for the optimization of administrative processes, mail processing and the digitization of analog archives and historical documents.

explainer.lead: Document processing turns paper and other analog documents into digital information that computers can understand, not just pictures of pages. It makes administrative work, mail handling, and historical archives easier to search, interpret, and use.

tiers.eli5: Scanning a page is like taking a photograph of a worksheet: you can see it, but the computer may not know what any of it says. Document processing goes further by finding the page’s parts, reading its writing, and collecting its pictures. It is a bit like turning a photographed worksheet into headings, answers, and images that a computer can work with.
tiers.practitioner: A typical pipeline digitizes pages, analyzes layout and content regions, then applies OCR, handwritten text recognition, or transcription before optional interpretation with NLP or image classification. Implementations can combine traditional computer vision, convolutional neural networks, and manual work. A common pitfall is treating a successful scan as a completed pipeline when structure and content have not yet been extracted.
tiers.paperLevel: For an analog document d, digitization produces an image I, while document processing additionally estimates a representation (L, C), where L denotes document structure or layout and C denotes textual or image content. The extraction and interpretation stages may involve semantic segmentation, object detection, OCR, HTR, transcription, NLP, or image classification, with automatic methods and manual labor both possible. Producing I alone does not establish that L or C has been recovered.

explainer.example: A scanned historical letter begins as a digital page image. Layout analysis identifies its writing regions, handwritten text recognition transcribes them, and any embedded images are extracted so the archive holds more than a photograph of the letter.

explainer.intuition: A page image preserves what a document looks like, but document processing aims to recover what it contains and how that content is organized. The goal is a digital representation that supports further interpretation, rather than pixels alone.
howItWorks: Digitize the analog document, often with a scanner.
Analyze its structure or layout using vision methods or manual work.
Locate and extract text and image content.
Recognize or transcribe text with OCR, HTR, or manual transcription.
Optionally interpret the result using NLP or image classification.
explainer.whyItMatters: It bridges physical documents and digital workflows by making their organization and content available to software. This supports administrative and mail processing as well as the digitization of archives and historical documents.
misconceptions: Scanning alone is not the whole process; the document must also become digitally intelligible.
Document processing is not limited to OCR; it can include layout analysis, image extraction, and interpretation.
It is not necessarily fully automatic, because manual labor can be part of the process.
